newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Warehouse says unsure why shares rising.
newsitem.headline: Warehouse says unsure why shares rising.

text.p: The Warehouse managing director Stephen Tindall said on Thursday was was unsure of the reason for the recent rise in his company's share price, the New Zealand Press Association reported.
On Wednesday The Warehouse closed 17 cents higher at NZ$3.57, up from $2.60 at the beginning of October.
"All I can put it down to, to be honest, is an air of optimism out there in the community that with the lowering of interest rates there's going to be a bit more spending," Tindall told NZPA.
While higher spending would flow through to the company's bottom line, Tindall said people's confidence was puzzling.

"I find it quite perplexing because we haven't got a government yet. I guess if one had asked this question a couple of months ago one could never have predicted this would happen, we are sitting here with no government, no direction."
Tindall would not be drawn on The Warehouse's sales as the company is reporting its quarterly sales figures next week.
"There were some obvious signs last year with huge amounts of stockpiling up at the back doors of our stores and being stored in car parks so you couldn't hide it.

"People could see that things were not working too well whereas this year the same people are still tramping the same tracks and they are obviously a little more comfortable with what they see," Tindall said.
